rationale: The board needs a summary of existing evidence before any local modelling, and one analyst can complete a systematic review in six months. The retrieved costing (c1) and model (c2) suggest budget impact estimates exist, so a random-effects meta-analysis of net annual budget impact per 100,000 population would give the board a single planning figure, with views of users and pharmacists summarised alongside.
alternatives: Rapid review of grey literature (refused: the decision justifies a full search)
Local budget impact model without a review (deferred: needs local data approval)
guidelines: CHEERS 2022 for reporting extracted economic data
whyNotMoreComplex: Primary data collection is outside the constraints; a review of existing studies is the simplest defensible input to the decision.

decision.statement: Conduct a systematic review with a random-effects meta-analysis of net annual budget impact per 100,000 population, with a narrative summary of views on how extended hours work.
decision.question: What should the authority commission to inform the March 2027 decision on extended pharmacy hours?

criteria.text: Published budget impact estimates exist for extended pharmacy opening.
The estimates are too few or too heterogeneous to pool.

gates.evidence: Commissioning plan line CP-2026-44, supplied by the investigator

decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 and c2; whether the estimates can be pooled is not yet assessed.

summary: Systematic review with meta-analysis of budget impact recommended; the decision rests on two ledger claims and its one gate is met.
